question: Does the publicly indexed LPPCHEA DENR Framework Plan or its JICA reproduction identify the underlying ERDB fish survey or independently corroborate the Ramsar list?

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed only the publicly indexed text and page metadata for a third-party hosted copy titled LPPCHEA Framework Plan Overview. The indexed cover identifies the DENR and partner institutions and the plan title. The host labels the copy all-rights-reserved; the original official-hosted PDF was not located and the copy was not downloaded or visually inspected.
relevantSections: Cover and document title: Saving the Last Coastal Frontier: Framework Plan for the Coastal Lagoons of Las Piñas and Parañaque.
Printed p. 15, section 3: Macro-invertebrate and Fish Species; the indexed text reports eight juvenile-to-sub-adult fish in the vicinity of LPPCHEA.
The paragraph does not state a survey year, methods, voucher basis, or direct fish-source citation.
sourceAccess.hostAndRightsCaveat: Third-party host only; no permission to reproduce the document or indexed species text was identified. Text extraction/OCR spellings have not been checked against a page image.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the official JICA final report through browser-extracted PDF text around its LPPCHEA environmental subsection.
relevantSections: PDF pp. 7-181 to 7-182, lines 7650-7663: states that eight juvenile fish were found around LPPCHEA and describes the area as nursery habitat.

The nearby source note explicitly names the DENR-NCR Framework Plan for adjacent ecological material, but its placement does not establish that the fish paragraph's exact lineage is the same plan or the same survey.

sourceAccess.accessMethod: Reviewed the 2014 Philippine Fifth National Report to the Convention on Biological Diversity bibliography entry naming the DENR Framework Plan.
relevantSections: Bibliography lists Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Framework Plan for the Coastal Lagoons of Las Piñas and Parañaque.
This supports the publication's bibliographic identity only; it does not validate the fish summary.

findings.statement: The indexed DENR Framework Plan text reports eight juvenile-to-sub-adult fish in the vicinity of LPPCHEA. The page credits the plan to DENR and partner institutions; independent bibliographic sources cite the plan as DENR (2012).
findings.evidenceType: Third-party indexed text for an apparent government framework plan, with its publication identity corroborated by independent bibliography entries.

findings.statement: The indexed plan text displays fish-name strings that differ from the Ramsar RIS in several places, including “Bathygodius forma fuscus,” “Valamugil cunesius,” “Sillago sihana,” “Sardinelle fimbria,” and “Gernes filamentousus.” These may be OCR or transcription forms; they have not been checked against the plan's printed page and must not be silently normalized or treated as verified specimen identities.
findings.evidenceType: Third-party indexed text only; not visually checked against the printed page.

findings.statement: JICA's later report also reports eight juvenile fish around LPPCHEA. It cites the DENR Framework Plan nearby for ecological material, but the fish paragraph has no explicit source citation and does not identify the underlying survey. This is repeated secondary context, not independent specimen or survey confirmation.
findings.evidenceType: Official JICA report text; source placement interpreted conservatively.

findings.statement: The searches located additional secondary summaries and a bibliographic reference to the DENR plan, but no directly reviewable 2001 ERDB field report, station-level data, or voucher-linked fish dataset.

lineageAssessment.relationshipToRamsarRis: The framework plan, Ramsar RIS, and JICA summaries share the LPPCHEA context and an eight-fish/juvenile-stage statement. Their detailed source linkage is not explicit enough to prove they describe the same sampling event or dataset. Treat the common count as overlapping secondary reporting, not independent validation.
lineageAssessment.frameworkPlanYear: Bibliographic sources cite the DENR plan as 2012; the indexed copy itself was not visually reviewed for a publication date.
lineageAssessment.jicaCitationScope: JICA explicitly cites the DENR Framework Plan around adjacent LPPCHEA ecological material. The source note's exact scope over the nearby fish sentence is unclear, so it is not treated as a confirmed fish-data lineage link.

limits: The DENR Framework Plan is available here only as a third-party indexed copy; its official full text and reuse terms were not established.
Fish-name strings from indexed text may contain OCR/transcription errors and remain unverified against the printed page.
Neither the Framework Plan nor the JICA summary supplies the original ERDB report, field methods, station/date details, effort, specimen counts, or voucher accessions in the reviewed passages.
The same aggregate count or juvenile-stage wording cannot prove that the secondary summaries use the same sample or independently validate fish identity.
No current occurrence, abundance, catchability, legal access, fish-safety, seasonality, or geometry claim is established.

decision.reason: Add the Framework Plan and its bibliographic/JICA references as secondary source-lineage material only. The primary ERDB study and the relationships among the secondary summaries remain unverified.

nextActions: Continue public-catalog and library searches for the official DENR Framework Plan and its source bibliography, without treating the third-party copy as publication clearance.
Search open ERDB research repositories and report catalogs for the specific 2001 LPPCHEA fish survey and an item that explicitly links it to the Framework Plan or the 2013 Ramsar RIS.
If a primary report is found, compare its printed fish names, survey date, stations, gear, effort, counts, vouchers, and reuse terms against the secondary summaries before any data admission.
Keep all summaries research-only; NCR and Luzon remain incomplete.

sources.supports: Third-party indexed copy of the LPPCHEA Framework Plan; its indexed text reports eight juvenile-to-sub-adult fish, but the source page was not visually checked and its reuse status is not cleared.
Official JICA report states an aggregate of eight juvenile fish around LPPCHEA and cites the DENR Framework Plan around neighboring ecological material; the specific fish lineage remains uncertain.
The 2014 Fifth National Report bibliography names the DENR Framework Plan for the Coastal Lagoons of Las Piñas and Parañaque.
Society for the Conservation of Philippine Wetlands conference material cites the Framework Plan as DENR (2012); it is bibliographic corroboration, not fish survey evidence.
